restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

This package is winglock's v14 (f1cedf6b, co-author Th0rgal) with two phases replaced by programs that compute the same outputs: T3 of the trail search P by meet-in-the-middle on zero blocks of alpha2 with a pigeonhole certification (proof 2.1; the zero-block half-sum match is Subflatus3's, 9bccf245, used there as a check), and E's stage 1 by the counted degree-4 fast exhaustive search of Bouillaguet et al. (CHES 2010), the function v14's evidence enumerator fes.c computed (proof 2.4). B', S, the connector, the driver, K = 96 and the caps X_MAX, S2CAP, B_BUDGET and CCAP are v14's, unchanged.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself, and its time is the sum of caps, fixed counts and organizer-recomputed counts times counted prices or stated bounds (proof 2, 6): P 2^30.03 units (T1, T2 as in v14; T3: 48,592,224 half vectors, 7 levels, 127 blocks, matches capped at M_CAP = 2^24); B' 2^32 units plus one update; at most 2^13 connector attempts of at most X_MAX = 2^23 work units; E: K = 96 spaces, setup at most 2^16 units, 2^24 Gray steps of 364 counted primitives per 256 pairs, at most S2CAP = 2^24 stage-2 pairs per space. Algorithm 2^33.9407.

Development is charged as preprocessing by v14's rule (proof 0.1, H2): every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number the algorithm reads, at the counted prices of the submitted programs. v14's G2 (2^31.8877) and C (2^33.2426), with their spaces at v15's E, and our D15 (2^34.6617: the abandoned contiguous-block T3 run charged as if completed, the layout comparison, the certified P run, checks). Total 2^35.7504, claimed 35.76; preprocessing 35.45. At v14's prices for G2 and C the total is 37.13, which does not improve on v14's 37.05: the claim rests on pricing development at the submitted programs, as v14's rule says.

Premise P (inside H1; success only): P outputs the trail of proof 3 within M_CAP. P's native run certified it at its level of 64 blocks (W* = 127 <= 2 x 64 - 1, Lemma P: every leaf with AS(alpha2) <= 63 is found, every other leaf has w1 >= 128), with 7,251,935 matches; the organizer recomputes the structural counts, the output core's level (r5-count trial 10), seed-picked cores (r5-mitm-0, 1) and P's driver on a sub-problem with its cap. If P certified nothing it would output nothing; every cost bound holds either way.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end (proof 5): R6, our pre-registration (plan and code hashed before any run, 48 complete runs of v15, all reported): 44 of 48 succeed, one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound 0.8193. R5, v14's pre-registration, consists of complete runs of v15 (Lemma 6): 46 of 48, bound 0.874. Claimed 0.40; each study alone supports it.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): R6 and R5 (proof 4.2, 4.7, Appendices D, E), with 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions as certificates; r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R5 successes per review; r5-bpfull runs a whole B' from its label; r5-count checks the counted stage 1 step by step against plain evaluation and its longest path, the T2 leaf, P's driver and cap, and P's certifying level on the output core; r5-trail-0..3 recount T1, T2 and the half vectors.

Th0rgal (7deb1595, with Subflatus3 and rubenmarcus) introduced the zero-advice framing; winglock's v8, v13, v14 built the algorithm this package modifies. Memory: largest phase about 2^28 bytes; declared 30.

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the counted programs and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v15's algorithm outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of each pre-registered study (R6, ours; R5, v14's) are an unselected sample of the algorithm's runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws. Premise P: P outputs the trail of proof Section 3 within M_CAP.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R6 run is a complete run of v15 with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6a: v14's B', connector and driver code, P's certified trail, E as fes with stage 2 and S2CAP; no cap that should not act acted), and each R5 run is one too (Lemma 6b: v15 computes v14's outputs). Premise P concerns success only: every cost term of P is a fixed count, an organizer-recomputed count or a cap. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R6: 44 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.8193, so by R6's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported. R5: 46 of 48, bound 0.8746. The studies are not pooled. Premise R: R6's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, enumerator and P program were hashed at 2026-10-08T00:19:33Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof 4.7, Appendix E: per-run ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; every other run made for v15 is listed (proof 4.1). Premise P: P's native run certifies the trail by Lemma P; it agrees with v14's exhaustive T3 passes; the organizer re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R5 as in v14 (r5-R-0..7, r5-bpfull); 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R6's failures, run order and timing are logged by us; the organizer re-derives no R6 run (the experiment file's 64-KiB budget holds only R5's table), but 7 R6 collisions are certificates. R5's limitations are v14's. P's full-scale certification rests on our native run (296 CPU-s, reproducible from Appendix A); the organizer checks 3 of 467 cores per review at the certifying level.

heuristics.statement: The charged development - v14's G2 (2^31.8877 units) and C (2^33.2426 units), priced at the counted prices of v15's programs, and our D15 (2^34.6617 units) - contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number that v15's algorithm reads, and these prices are the ones the cost model requires. Every other run either produced program text or fixed no number of v15.
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^33.9407) are caps, fixed counts and recomputed counts at counted prices or stated bounds, and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1 lists every run with what it fixed and the claim it would give if charged (A1 40.98, A2 38.44, R5 36.23, R6 36.44, C' 41.24, D at most 36.93, A3/A4 37.28, v14's native T3 runs 36.52). Proof 0.2 gives the origin of every new number of v15: analysis, counting, or a charged run (D15). G2 and C are priced at v15's E by v14's own rule (the search, if added to the submitted program, runs on its counted routines); C's spaces were computed by fes.c, which is v15's stage 1. D15 charges our abandoned contiguous-block T3 run as if its last level had completed (its match count recounted without enumeration) and every other development run of v15 at P's prices.
heuristics.limitations: At v14's prices for G2 and C the total is 37.13, above v14's 37.05: the improvement depends on accepting v14's pricing rule for development as applied to v15's programs. A1 (v7's design study that produced B''s code) stays uncharged as in v14; charging it gives 40.98. D15's largest item is an upper bound (the stopped run is charged complete).
